clue.text: Artist in Baltic country volunteers for operatic work

indicators.note: the artist sits inside the name of the Baltic country, so these letters go within it

parts.note: Latvia is one of the three Baltic states
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword stock artist
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A painter living in Latvia joins volunteers working on an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera about the courtesan Violetta is a celebrated example of an operatic work.

clue.text: Cover placed over old swimming pool

indicators.note: in a down entry, the cover being placed over means it sits above the next piece

parts.note: a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: Someone puts a cover over an old, disused swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-air public bathing place is called this in British usage, after the Venice beach.

clue.text: Climber to catch up on most of exercises

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written on another sits above it
in a down entry, going up means the word for catch is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it

indicators.note: most of the word means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: drill is a set of training exercises

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to catch up on most of their exercise routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant's thin coiling shoot that grips supports is how a climbing plant climbs, so it is a climber.

clue.text: Still together

definitions.meaning: still in the sense of nevertheless, as in 'but all the same'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both nevertheless, like 'still', and simultaneously, like 'together'.

clue.text: Diamonds put on top of carton in compartment of fridge

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting one piece on top of another places it above

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
a box is a carton

explanation.surface: Jewels are hidden on top of a carton in the fridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The freezing section inside a refrigerator is known by this name, especially in older usage.

clue.text: Easy shot bagging stray reptile

indicators.note: bagging means holding inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a tap-in is an easy goal or putt from close range
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A hunter takes an easy shot at a stray reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater turtle is a reptile, as are all turtles and tortoises.

clue.text: I study computer symbol

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Someone is studying a symbol on a computer screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A small picture on a screen standing for a program or file is a computer symbol.

clue.text: Check complicated lease in residential district of London

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

indicators.note: complicated means the letters of the word lease are tangled up into a new order

explanation.surface: A tenant is told to check a complicated lease for a London flat.
explanation.definitionFit: This affluent area of west London, by the Thames, is a well-known residential district.

clue.text: Little Eleanor and Daniel covering English music hall song

parts.note: Nellie is a pet form of the name Eleanor

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the short name goes outside the letter for English

explanation.surface: Two singers called Eleanor and Daniel perform an old English music hall number.
explanation.walkthrough: Music hall was the popular British variety theatre of the late 1800s and early 1900s; this sentimental song from 1905 became a singalong standard.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1905 ballad by Harry Armstrong is a famous music hall song, a fixture of pub singalongs.

clue.text: Place to eat? Daughter and I clear end of table

parts.note: nett means clear, as in clear profit after deductions

indicators.note: end of means just the last letter of the word table is used

explanation.surface: A daughter and her parent clear the end of the dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dining area or alcove off a kitchen is a place to eat, hence the question mark for a less obvious example.

clue.text: Unfair treatment in chilly and damp Kent town

parts.note: raw weather is cold and damp
Deal is a seaside town in the English county of Kent

explanation.surface: A visitor complains of being treated badly in a cold, wet Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting a bad bargain or harsh handling is an idiom for unfair treatment.

clue.text: Aggressive type set out to bring about industrial action

parts.note: a wildcat is a fierce, quick-tempered person
to strike, as in strike north, is to set out in a direction

explanation.surface: A militant sets out to provoke a walkout at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden walkout without union approval is a form of industrial action, a British term for strikes.

clue.text: Contest open to anybody — no entry fee?

definitions.meaning: a brawl or competition anyone may join
read literally, admission costing nothing for everyone

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an unrestricted scramble and, read word by word, free admission to everyone.

clue.text: Leave out incomplete piece of sports equipment

indicators.note: incomplete means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to skip something is to leave it out

explanation.surface: Someone omits an unfinished piece of sports kit from their packing.
explanation.definitionFit: A long runner for gliding over snow is a piece of sports equipment.

clue.text: Talk up opinion about a cable TV service

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first pieces surround the word for a
in a down entry, up means the word for talk is read bottom to top

parts.note: to yap is to talk noisily
a view is an opinion
per means a, as in so much per head or a head

explanation.surface: Someone talks up their opinion of a cable television channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A system where viewers pay for each programme they watch is a cable or satellite TV service.

clue.text: At sea in a launch

parts.note: to float a company is to launch it

explanation.surface: A sailor is out at sea in a motor launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launch' looks like a boat, but it is the verb, as in launching a company on the stock market.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the water rather than ashore is being at sea; both also mean buoyant.

clue.text: Soft, the Italian vegetable and fish

parts.note: P is piano, the musical abbreviation for soft
il is Italian for the
chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: An Italian cook serves soft vegetables with fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily sea fish of the herring family, like an adult sardine, is a fish.

clue.text: Discharge spray can in this manner inside

parts.note: a jet is a spray of liquid

indicators.note: inside means the phrase for in this manner goes within the word for can

parts.note: a tin is a can
so means in this way or thus

explanation.surface: Instructions for an aerosol: discharge the spray can like this, from inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing cargo overboard to lighten a ship is a sense of discharge, getting rid of a load.

clue.text: Eyeglasses suitable for the likes of van Gogh, ultimately?

definitions.text: Eyeglasses suitable for the likes of van Gogh, ultimately?

parts.words: Eyeglasses suitable for the likes of van Gogh, ultimately?
parts.note: glasses clipped to the nose, with no arms resting on the ears, would suit a painter who in the end had cut off an ear

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which spectacles would have suited the Dutch painter van Gogh.
explanation.walkthrough: Van Gogh famously cut off part of his ear late in his life, so 'ultimately' he would need glasses that do not hook over the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: These are spectacles held in place by a spring gripping the bridge of the nose, so they are eyeglasses.

clue.text: Famous father's come in for item of stationery

indicators.note: the father has come in, so his letters go inside the word for famous

parts.note: noted means famous
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A well-known father has come in to buy stationery.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of paper for jotting down notes is an item of stationery.

clue.text: Brand new mag after it's found backing

indicators.note: the rearranged magazine word comes after the reversed piece
backing means the letters of it's are read in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: new means the letters of mag are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A brand-new magazine is found to have financial backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark of disgrace is a brand, in the sense of a stain on one's reputation.

clue.text: Joke about line written on black potting compost container

indicators.note: the joke goes about, or around, the other pieces

parts.note: a gag is a joke

indicators.note: in a down entry, the line written on black sits above it

parts.note: a row is a line
B is the pencil-lead abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A gardener jokes about a line written on a black compost sack.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is a plastic sack of compost laid flat, slit open and planted straight into.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bag of potting compost in which plants such as tomatoes are grown, so a compost container.

clue.text: Solitary single only

definitions.meaning: solitary means the sole one of its kind
single means being one of a kind
only means without equal, the sole one

explanation.definitionFit: Being the one and only of its kind is the shared sense of solitary, single and only.

clue.text: Corruption — zero tolerance cases

indicators.note: the words zero tolerance act as cases holding the answer's letters within them

explanation.surface: Authorities pledge zero tolerance in corruption cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot means decay, and figuratively moral decay or corruption.

clue.text: Speech pattern not uncommon in one state

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go in among the pieces for one and state

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a nation is a state

indicators.note: uncommon means the letters of not are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A linguist notes a speech pattern that is fairly common in one state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not uncommon' reads as the familiar phrase for 'fairly common', but the two words split: 'not' is the fodder and 'uncommon' says to shuffle it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rise and fall of the voice in speaking is a speech pattern.

clue.text: Netting's border raised across third of base

indicators.note: the reversed border lies across, or around, the picked letter
in a down entry, raised means the word for border is read upwards

parts.note: a hem is a border of cloth

indicators.note: third of means the third letter of the word base

explanation.surface: A net's border is lifted across a third of a base.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesh is a synonym for netting, an openwork fabric of threads.

clue.text: Have a favourable effect on independent politician on steamship

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: An independent politician aboard a steamship tries to make a good impression.
explanation.definitionFit: To win admiration from someone is to make a favourable impact on them.

clue.text: Revised edition of bible after question results in minor criticism

indicators.note: the rearranged book comes after the question
a revised edition reworks the text, so the letters of bible are rearranged

explanation.surface: Questioning a revised Bible edition only leads to petty complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty objection over a trivial point is a minor criticism.

clue.text: Extra fish got by wife

indicators.note: the fish is got by, next to, the wife, which comes first

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A wife catches an extra fish.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a ball bowled too far from the batter is a run-scoring 'extra' added to the total.
explanation.definitionFit: This cricket delivery out of the batter's reach counts as one of the extras, runs not scored off the bat.

clue.text: Like some skirts in joint, to an extent?

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
length is extent in space

explanation.surface: Some skirts reach a joint of the leg, to some extent.
explanation.definitionFit: A hemline reaching the knee describes certain skirts, so this is a description of some skirts.
